newsitem.title: INDIA: BA says India flights partially resume.
newsitem.headline: BA says India flights partially resume.

text.p: British Airways said on Thursday that it had resumed flights operating from London to Delhi, Calcutta and Dhaka following the return to duty of a large number of cabin crew members from a strike.

On Wednesday the airline was forced to cancel half of its flights out of London and up to 30 percent of the 1,000 flights it operates worldwide each day because of a strike by its cabin crew, which entered its second day on Thursday.
The crew called the strike over allowances and overtime and in protest against airline's plans to cut 42 million pounds ($71 million) from its operating budget.
"With a large number of crew coming to work, we are able to operate many of our flights to and from India," Kevin Steele, British Airways' general manager, South Asia, said in a statement.
The statement quoted Steele as saying the airline hoped to resume normal operations soon.
British Airways operates a daily flight out of Delhi and Bombay to London, two flights a week out of Calcutta and Madras to London, and five flights a week from Delhi to Dhaka.
BA said cargo operations carried along with passenger load would also be hit by the strike. The airline carries about 250 tonnes of cargo out of India each week.
